question: Was the original success direction a harmless notation error or a genuine ambiguity in the decision rule?
prior_working_record_states: The earlier draft described the residual contrast as B3 - B5. That text is reported in the prior phase record but is not recoverable from Git and cannot be independently timestamped.

committed_protocol_evidence.line_97: Energy is lower-is-better, so the positive advantage is defined as B5 energy - B3 energy; positive means B3 is better.
committed_protocol_evidence.lines_100_101: This is a sign-convention clarification; the target quantity (whether B3 has lower energy than B5) is unchanged.
committed_protocol_evidence.line_159: G4 is defined as B5-10 - B3 H20 energy mean > 0, block-5 95% CI low > 0, fraction better > 0.5.

reasoning: The committed protocol defines a physically unambiguous target: lower energy is better and B3 must have lower energy.
However, the only committed protocol was added in the same commit as the results; there is no independently timestamped pre-evaluation protocol commit.
The protocol itself records that the sign was clarified, so the written decision rule was not frozen unambiguously before the observed contrast was interpreted.
The numerical contrast is unchanged by the notation, but it cannot be called a fully prespecified confirmatory PASS.
note: This decision downgrades evidential status only. It does not alter the computed energies, interval, win rate, or gate arithmetic.
